## When you'd use this

<UseCases>
<UseCase title="A section with its own heading">
Put the questions about an emergency contact together under "Emergency contact", as in the example above. The group's label is the section's heading.
</UseCase>
<UseCase title="Several questions that show together">
Give the group a condition, and every question in it shows or hides with it, such as a "Parent or guardian" group shown only when the respondent is under 18.
</UseCase>
<UseCase title="Sections within sections">
Put a group inside another group. Groups nest up to 20 deep.
</UseCase>
</UseCases>

When the questions are to be answered once per person, item or visit, use a [repeating group](/docs/build/structure/repeating-groups) instead.

## Before you start

- You need a form open in the editor.
- A group must hold at least one block before the form can be saved. Add the group first, then the questions in it.
- A group collects no answer of its own. It has no Required and no Help text, isn't numbered, and can't be the source of a condition.

## Steps

1. Below the last block, select **+** (Insert a block), or type `/` in the line beside it.
2. Under **Structure**, choose **Group**. Typing `section` finds it too. An empty group, "Untitled group", is added and selected.
3. In **Label**, write the group's heading.
4. With the group selected, insert blocks as usual: each one is added at the end of the group. With a block inside the group selected, the next one goes right after it.
5. To bring in a block that is already on the form, drag it into the group by its handle (**Drag to reorder**), or select it and, under **Position**, choose the group in **Move to…** and select **Move**.
6. Select **Save**.
<Gif alt="Adding a group and putting questions in it" />

<Note>
To take a block out of a group, choose **Top level (outside any group)** in **Move to…**, or drag it out.
</Note>

To delete a group, select it and choose **Delete group…**. The builder asks what to do with what is inside:

| Choice | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Group only (keep questions)** | The group goes, and its contents move up to where the group was, in the same order. Its own conditions stop applying to them. |
| **Group and its questions** | The group and everything in it are deleted. |

## What happens behind the scenes

- **The group is shown as a section:** its label is a heading, with its questions under it. In a form without pages a group's heading is level 2; in a form with pages, level 3, under the page title. Each group inside another is one level lower, down to level 6.
- **A group's conditions apply to everything in it.** A question shows only when its own conditions pass and every group around it is showing.
- **A group that shows nothing is hidden,** heading and all: when every block in it is hidden by its conditions, or shows nothing, such as an empty Text block.
- **Groups don't change the answers.** Each question's answer is sent under its own id, as if the group weren't there.

## Rules the builder enforces

| What you try | What the builder says |
|---|---|
| Save a group with no blocks in it | Group "Emergency contact": a group must contain at least one block. |
| Save a group with an empty label | An unlabelled group at the top level: a group needs a label. (the start says where the group is) |
| Save a group inside 20 other groups | Group "Section › … › Details": groups can be nested at most 20 deep, and this group is inside 20 others. Move it up a level. (the start names every group around it) |
| Delete a group and its questions, when a question outside it has a condition on one inside | Can't delete "Emergency contact" and its questions — these questions outside it have conditions that depend on something inside it: |

The names in quotation marks are examples; the builder uses yours.

## Troubleshooting

**The form won't save, and points at the group.** The group is empty. Add a block to it, or delete it.

**A question inside the group never shows.** The group itself is hidden by its conditions, or by those of a group around it. Check each one.

**A group isn't offered as the source of a condition.** Groups can't be sources. Use one of the questions inside it.
